setup: Stand tall with your feet roughly shoulder-width apart and your toes angled slightly outward.
Brace your core and extend your arms in front of your chest for balance.
steps: Initiate the descent by breaking simultaneously at the hips and knees.
Lower your body slowly over a strict three-second count until your hip crease drops below the top of your knees.
Pause motionless in the bottom position for a full one-second count without losing core tension.
Drive through your midfoot to stand up at a normal, controlled speed.
Fully extend your hips and knees at the top before beginning the next repetition.
instructions.breathing: Inhale deeply into your abdomen on the slow descent, hold your breath through the pause, and exhale as you drive back to standing.
cues: Count your descent: three, two, one.
Keep your chest proud and knees tracking your toes.

common_faults.fault: Rushing the eccentric tempo as fatigue sets in.
common_faults.correction: Use an internal or audible metronome count to ensure a true three-second descent on every rep.

common_faults.fault: Collapsing tension or bouncing out of the bottom position.
common_faults.correction: Stay actively braced and come to a complete, controlled stop for the prescribed pause.

common_faults.fault: Heels lifting off the floor during the descent.
common_faults.correction: Maintain balanced pressure across your entire foot, driving knees outward to make room for hip depth.

precautions: Descend only to a depth you can maintain with a neutral spine.

name: Bodyweight Tempo Squat
summary: A bilateral bodyweight squat performed with an intentionally slowed eccentric phase and a brief pause at the bottom to maximize time under tension and movement control.
